lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives. 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. The only researcher entry (Gowans $20, two mixed resin figures incl a G Armani figure) was dropped as not the same item. WebSearch was capped this turn, so no Armitage, Invaluable or dealer comparables could be found.
lots.working: No surviving SOLD entry for an Armani figural lamp, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. Gowans figural lamps (category only, not Armani) mostly hammer $10 to $380 (e.g. 'FIGURAL LADY LAMP' $300, Dec 2025, a bronze-look resin lamp), which says only that decorative figure lamps sell modestly in Tasmania.
lots.confidence_reason: Mark read clearly in photo 3 (signature 'Giuseppe Armani', (c) 1998 Florence, blue crown-N mark) but zero sold, unsold or asking evidence survived. Web search budget exhausted.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: Gowans $20 hammer, listed 2026-02-23, '2 RESIN FIGURES INCL G ARMANI & KANREX FIGURE' (API JSON opened and confirmed: sale_price 2000, bid_count 0). Not the same item: a two-figure mixed lot, not a lamp, Armani figure unidentified, no bids recorded. Not a usable comparable. Also checked Gowans 'armani lamp', 'giuseppe armani', 'florence figure', 'figurine lamp' (no results) and 'figural lamp' (30 lots, none Armani; photos of the top three checked, all generic bronze-look lamps).
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3 base clearly reads 'Giuseppe Armani' in script, '(c) 1998 FLORENCE', with the blue crown over N mark used on Florence Sculture d'Arte pieces. Figure looks intact in the photos, fingers, dog and hat brim visible with no obvious breaks. Plinth glossy with a small brass plaque. Shade looks clean. Australian plug fitted.
lots.condition: Appears good from three photos, no chips or breaks seen, but small resin details (hands, dog, hat flower) need a close look; electrical condition and test-and-tag unknown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is the figure free of chips, cracks or repairs (hands, dog, hat brim), does the lamp work and is it tested and tagged, and is the shade original or a replacement? Is there a model number or title under the plinth?

lots.working: No surviving SOLD evidence for a signed Giovanni Cenedese engraved clear vase, so both maximums are 0. For context only, Gowans coloured Murano-type vases hammer $60 to $110 (premium extra), and clear engraved glass would normally sit below coloured sommerso pieces.
lots.confidence_reason: Signature read but its authenticity is unproven, the attribution rests on a handwritten dealer-style sticker, and no comparable evidence survived.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped all three (Gowans API JSON opened and figures confirmed): $65 'MURANO GLASS 2 HANDLED VASE' listed 2025-10-19; $90 'MURANO GREEN GLASS VASE' listed 2026-03-23; $110 'MURANO STYLE ART GLASS VASE' listed 2026-05-03. Prices and dates match the researcher, but none is the same item (coloured or 'style' pieces, not a signed clear engraved vase), so they are category context only. Gowans searches for 'cenedese', 'engraved glass vase' and 'italian glass vase' returned nothing; 'etched glass vase' gave unrelated pieces.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged base shows an engraved script signature reading 'Cenedese Giovanni' and a small sans-serif etched block reading roughly 'O82FHG / LIMITED / EDITION' (looks machine or stencil etched, more like a modern production mark than a studio signature). Handwritten sticker says 'Vintage Murano engraver Giovanni Cenedese'. Clear glass only, no colour. Light base scratching. A '4711' sticker near the rim.
lots.condition: Appears sound, light wear and scratches to the base, no chips seen in two photos; rim not shown close up.
lots.question_for_armitage: Any chips to the rim or base edge, and what is the height? Does the 'Limited Edition' mark include an edition number?

lots.key_photo_findings: One photo only. Enlarged view shows an illusion-set cluster of about 7 to 9 small single-cut diamonds or white stones on an engagement ring with a crossover or twist shoulder, sitting against a plain polished band of the same colour. Gold looks yellow with a rose tint. No hallmark, carat stamp or maker's mark visible. No obvious missing stones or damage seen at this resolution.
lots.condition: Looks good and lightly worn from one photo; stones appear all present. Metal, fineness, weight, size and whether the two rings are joined or separate are unknown.
lots.question_for_armitage: What are the hallmarks on both rings (9ct, 375, 18ct or plated), the total weight in grams and the ring size? Are the two rings separate or soldered together, and are the stones diamonds, all present and secure?
